annotations.title: Check videos against each place's limits

description: Use it when the user wants a video checked against a place's limits, or burned captions against a phone app's safe area. Measures finished MP4 files against each place's published limits without changing them: shape, size, frame rate, length, file size, codecs, and whether the MP4 is whole and laid out as Instagram and YouTube ask. Give it a folder reframe_video made, its formats.json, or one MP4 with the places in for. With captions, the ASS, SRT or WebVTT file burned into the video, it checks their timing, and an ASS file's text against each 9:16 place's safe area. It writes CHECK.md, which the result shows, and check.json. A failed check is a normal result, with what failed and the limit's source. It does not say whether a video may be posted. For loudness, black, still and silent stretches, use check_video instead. The reframe playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (reframekit 0.1.3, on this machine.)

captions.description: The ASS, SRT or WebVTT file of the captions burned into the video: its timing is checked, and an ASS file's text against each 9:16 place's safe area. caption_video writes captions.ass beside its captioned.mp4.

for.description: The places to check a lone MP4 against, any of tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube, x, linkedin, feed and square (default: the places of its shape); with a folder, only these.

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-4a3i6zrn. Default: <target-folder>/reframekit-check-<target-name>, where <target-name> is the name of target without its extension and <target-folder> is the folder target is in.

target.description: What to check: a folder reframe_video made, its formats.json, or one MP4, like captioned.mp4.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

name: check_place_limits

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.
